notes:
PPI checklist (2026-10-08) — BMW-experienced shop WITH A LIFT; cold start (seller not to warm it up); photos + a call with the tech.
1. Rear structure: battery box + tool tray out; diff-mount spot welds in the trunk floor; from below: subframe mounts, diff ears, subframe-to-body; cracks / old repairs / any reinforcement.
2. Cooling (no records in 26 yrs, long storage): pressure test; water pump play/weep; expansion tank, radiator necks, thermostat housing; fan clutch; coolant; any overheat history.
3. Front damage: lower lip torn; bumper support; radiator + A/C condenser behind it.
4. Gouged front wheel: balancer, check bend / crack near the spoke (seller says not cracked).
5. Identity: VIN [VIN] on windshield, door jamb, frame = the Arkansas title; LSD (diff tag or lift-and-turn test); engine is the original S52, unmodified.
6. CA smog: stored/pending codes, readiness monitors; original cats, stock exhaust.
7. Engine/drivetrain: VANOS rattle/codes; leaks (valve cover, oil filter housing, pan, rear main); clutch slip/engagement; gearbox/shifter; belts, pulleys, hose age.
8. Suspension/brakes: rear shock mounts (Z3 failure point); front control-arm + rear trailing-arm bushings; sway links; pads/rotors/fluid.
9. Body/top/interior: paint meter on every panel; rust (trunk battery area, floors — 16 yrs Arkansas); soft top + rear window + frame; window regulators; electrics/gauges; tire date codes.
Ask for: buy/don't-buy verdict; must-fix vs can-wait; rough cost for every finding.
TITLE (separate from the PPI): seller's name is not on the title (AR title -> donor parent -> school -> seller). Get photos of front+back of the title + donation + notarized purchase docs, and check with a CA registration service BEFORE paying anything.

contradictions.detail: The listing header says '2000 BMW z3 3.0i Roadster' while the description says '2000 Z3M Roadster'. The VIN decode (Z3 M, 3.2L) and the photos settle it as an M Roadster.

The seller says the title was signed 'from I think original owner' to the donor parent. CARFAX shows 4 owners, with the last titled owner in Arkansas 2005-2021. The car then went through a MO dealer pre-purchase inspection (08/2021) and BMW Seattle service (2021-2024) with no WA title ever recorded. The seller is not the titled owner, and the paperwork chain to him is unverified.

critical_evidence.evidence: The seller's trunk photos and video show a clean floor, no rust, no lifted sealer and no reinforcement plates in the areas shown. The floor under the battery box and tool tray, the differential-mount spot welds and the underside were not shown. CARFAX has no subframe or reinforcement entry.

CARFAX has no reported cooling entry across 17 service records. The seller says 'No work I am aware of.' There is no evidence of a water pump, radiator, expansion tank or thermostat replacement in 26 years.
This is a 2000 model-year US M Roadster with the S52 3.2L, confirmed by VIN decode and CARFAX. The S54 rod-bearing issue does not apply.

documentation.rationale: Identity is settled: the VIN decodes to an S52 Z3 M, and a CARFAX shows 17 BMW-dealer service entries, no brands and consistent odometer readings. The partial trunk photos are a start. The gaps: no invoices; no cooling, VANOS or subframe documentation; a 12-year stretch with only registrations; and a title the seller does not hold, with the donation chain documents unseen.

condition.rationale: Photos show a straight, clean car with a tidy black M interior, an intact soft top and a clean trunk in the areas shown. Observed defects: the disclosed front bumper / lower-lip damage and a gouge on a front wheel near a spoke (seller says it is not cracked). Cooling and rear structure are unproven either way.

price_value.rationale: $14,000 is about 20% below the low end of the $17,595-$22,455 fair-value range for a 54k-mile S52 roadster. That is pulled down by cosmetic known work (bumper lip, wheel), probable cooling catch-up and the friction of an unresolved title chain.

mission_fit.rationale: It fits the keeper brief well: an S52 (the preferred engine), manual, low mileage, mostly stock, and priced inside the ideal band, so it does not strain cash. It is a keeper rather than a bridge, though as a usable roadster it could serve both roles.

logistics.rationale: The car is in Poulsbo/Seattle, a fly-up-and-drive-home trip. The seller offers a PPI before money moves. California registration depends on resolving an untransferred Arkansas title through a donation chain, which needs paperwork verification first.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: S52 M Roadster with a manual, low mileage, OEM wheels and an apparently stock M interior. Silver over black is a common rather than rare combination.

evidence.mission_note: As a future keeper, this S52 manual M Roadster at $14,000 fits the brief and the ideal budget band rather than straining cash preservation. Its appeal depends on the title chain and the rear structure checking out.
evidence.rationale: The VIN and CARFAX establish a 2000 S52 Z3 M Roadster with a manual, no reported brands or accidents, a consistent odometer, and dealer service through 06/2024 at 49,055 miles. Observed problems are cosmetic: disclosed front bumper / lower-lip damage and a gouged front wheel, which the seller says is not cracked. The material issue is paperwork. The seller is not the titled owner, the last title is Arkansas, and the car passed through an untitled 2021 purchase, a donor parent and a school before reaching him. CARFAX shows no cooling, VANOS or subframe work, plus a 12-year stretch with registrations only, so age-related rubber and plastics are likely original. The seller's trunk photos show a clean floor but not the diff-mount welds or the underside, so rear structure remains open. At $14,000 the car sits well below the $17,595-$22,455 fair-value range.
evidence.next_action: Ask the seller for photos of the assigned Arkansas title (front and back), the donation acknowledgment and the notarized contract, and check them with the CA DMV before booking a BMW-specialist PPI that covers the diff-mount welds and cooling system.
